For exact zero initialization, use a directly optimized `alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.))`; after `optimizer.step()`, execute `with torch.no_grad(): alpha.clamp_(0., 2.)`. This projects the parameter after updating, leaving the forward gradient intact ([projected optimization](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs4220/2026sp/lec/2026-04-27.html)). Smooth alternative: `alpha=2*sigmoid(raw)`, initialized with `raw=log(epsilon/(2-epsilon))` for small positive epsilon ([PyTorch sigmoid](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.Sigmoid.html)). Mathematical limitation: a differentiable nonnegative parameterization attaining zero at a finite interior point must have zero derivative there; exact zero plus a nonzero ordinary gradient requires projection or another boundary treatment.

Uncorrected negative-sampling BCE learns a data-versus-noise score: under idealized sampling, `s*(h,i)=log p(i|h)-log(k*q(i|h))`, rather than a calibrated catalog probability ([candidate-sampling derivation](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf)). Consequently, transition probabilities and SASRec logits need compatible scales. Suggested implementation: use a bounded/log-transformed transition feature with fixed training-derived scaling, train the combined logit, and select scaling using validation. Sampling exclusions and loss weighting modify the ideal formula; avoid adding a correction only during inference.

For sparse transitions, proposed implementation: encode edges as sorted int64 keys `source*num_items+destination`; use batched `torch.searchsorted`, guard out-of-range positions, verify equality, and return zero for missing edges ([API](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.searchsorted.html)). Query only positive/negative items at each causal training position. For full-catalog inference, aggregate recent-source CSR rows into a batch-by-catalog buffer, or use sparse multiplication ([API](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.sparse.mm.html)). Share causal history weighting, normalization, padding rules, alpha, and transition buffers between training and the exported predictor; verify candidate scores equal indexed full-catalog scores.
